summary: After the semiconductor index fell ~20% into a bear market, Brian argues the selloff dragged strong AI builders down with the overvalued names and presents ten picks trading below their worth. Sterling Infrastructure (STRL, BUY): data-center site work is ~70% of revenue and grew 174%, with $5.15B backlog against $2.49B of revenue and a PEG near 0.88. Oracle (ORCL, BUY): halved from ~$279 on capex fears but sitting on $638B of signed contracts (~10x last year's sales), with free cash flow expected to flip positive within two years. Modine (MODN, HOLD): the full-stack liquid-cooling play with a $4B+ customer commitment, fairly priced at PEG ~0.6. Broadcom (AVGO, BUY): AI revenue nearly tripling, $73B in booked AI orders, ~24x forward earnings once VMware amortization is stripped out, PEG ~0.5. Lumentum (LITE, BUY): the EML laser choke point — Nvidia invested $2B and designated its optics for the Rubin platform. Credo (CRDO, BUY): owns ~88% of active electrical cables, revenue up 206%, margins flipped to 33%. SanDisk (SNDK, BUY): its High-Bandwidth-Flash could double its market, trading under 10x next year's earnings. Tower Semiconductor (TSEM, BUY): the silicon-photonics foundry with $1.3B of 2027 orders already booked. Cohu (COHU, BUY): a cyclical tester with a ~$750M AI pipeline. Innodata (INOD, BUY): the data-labeling name whose fraud accusations collapsed with regulators taking no action. His sizing rule: heavy on mega caps scaling down to small caps — asymmetric by design.
title: Everyone Sold Last Week. That Was The Mistake
